intro.text: Other main systems after Black asks the bishop: modern active bishop lines, the solid Steinitz setups, early protecting moves for White and less common knight moves.
Black asks the bishop to decide at once. Most strong players retreat it to keep the Spanish pressure; the exchange gives the Exchange Variation.
White keeps the pin by retreating the bishop rather than exchanging. This is the main move of the Ruy Lopez and leads to most of the famous systems.
Black develops the knight and attacks the centre pawn, the main position of the Ruy Lopez. White most often castles, letting Black choose between the open and closed systems.
Black protects the centre pawn with a pawn before developing the king's knight, a solid setup where Black can choose between holding and releasing the centre.
Black develops the king's knight to a modest square to keep the f-pawn free and avoid pins. Unusual but playable.
Black gains queenside space early and drives the bishop back, at the cost of slightly loosening the queenside.
Black fianchettoes the dark-squared bishop after questioning the white bishop, aiming for a solid setup that eyes the centre from a distance.
White protects the centre pawn with a pawn before castling, a calm modern setup that keeps many options and avoids early forcing play.
White develops the queen's knight early to protect the centre pawn, keeping the position simple and flexible.
Against the Cozio setup White prepares a big centre with pawns. Black usually fianchettoes and tries to hold the centre with pieces.

intro.text: White exchanges the bishop one move later than in the Exchange Variation, after Black has developed the knight. Black recaptures and has easy development.

black.text: Black's winners castled long with O-O-O, pinned with Bg4 and stormed with h5 and g5 against White's king.

intro.text: Black protects the centre pawn with a pawn after the knight is out, a solid but slightly passive system that often leads to a kingside fianchetto.
Against the quiet protecting move Black drives the bishop to the long diagonal first, keeping options for the dark-squared bishop.
Black develops the dark-squared bishop to its most active diagonal before castling, inviting White to build a big centre with gain of time.
Black supports the knight with the bishop, breaking the pin and preparing a solid kingside development. White gets a free hand in the centre.
Black supports the centre with a pawn and keeps the bishop flexible, aiming for a compact kingside development.

black.text: Black's winners struck at White's centre with the f-pawn advance f5.

intro.text: Black develops the bishop actively against the quiet setup, aiming at White's kingside. Play is slow and positional.
Against the knight development Black drives the bishop away first, gaining queenside space before deciding on the centre.
Black chases the bishop and offers to trade knight for bishop at once. It is a concrete line where White can try to trap or exploit Black's loose queenside.
Black counter-attacks in the centre with the f-pawn, a sharp idea that opens lines towards White's king at the cost of loosening Black's own.

white.text: White's winners exploited the light squares weakened by Black's f-pawn: the bishop returned to Bb3 and the queen came to Qb3 or Qd5.

intro.text: White prepares a central pawn advance that will hit Black's bishop. Black usually expands on the queenside first to keep the bishop active.
White protects the centre pawn with the rook against the solid deferred Steinitz setup, preparing a central advance with the pawns.
White builds a solid central pawn structure and keeps a retreat for the bishop. Black often fianchettoes.
White prepares a central advance against the solid modern Steinitz setup, with a comfortable space advantage.
White grips the centre with pawns, preventing Black's central break. A slow, space-gaining plan.

white.text: White's winners exchanged with Bxc6 and prepared d4 with b3 to open the centre.

black.text: Black's winners occupied the hole in White's camp with Nd4, which White's pawns can no longer drive away.

intro.text: Black develops the dark-squared bishop actively after gaining queenside space, aiming at White's kingside and the centre. Sharp, modern and very popular among strong players.
